name: Lhasa
tagline: The holy city of Tibetan Buddhism
summary: At 3,650 m on the Tibetan plateau, Lhasa is the spiritual heart of Tibetan Buddhism. Pilgrims walk clockwise around the Jokhang Temple and spin prayer wheels below the Potala Palace, the former winter home of the Dalai Lamas, while great monasteries like Sera and Drepung sit on the hills around the city.
seasonNote: April to June and September to October are clear and mild. July and August are the busiest and wettest. Winter is cold but sunny and quiet. Tibet often closes to foreign visitors for weeks around February and March, and around sensitive dates, so check before you book.
arrival: Foreign visitors need a Tibet Travel Permit as well as a Chinese visa, and must travel on a guided tour booked with a licensed agency, which arranges the permit and meets you at the airport or station. Independent travel is not allowed. Fly from Chengdu, Beijing or Kathmandu, or take the train from Xining (about 22 hours). The altitude is 3,650 m: rest on the first day, drink water and avoid alcohol.
gettingAround: Your guide and driver take you between sights; the old town around the Barkhor is walkable.
cashTip: Carry yuan; mobile payments (Alipay, WeChat Pay) are everywhere, and foreign cards work only in bigger hotels.
foodTip: Momos, thukpa noodle soup, tsampa (roasted barley flour), yak meat and salty butter tea in old town teahouses.
buyTip: Prayer flags, thangka paintings, incense, yak-wool shawls and Tibetan jewellery around the Barkhor.
baseArea: Old town near the Barkhor and Jokhang

connections.note: Seasonal flights; a Tibet group visa is issued in Kathmandu for this route.
Some flights stop in Chengdu or Xining.
Usually with a stop; the train via Xining takes about two days.

items.name: Potala Palace
items.summary: The towering white and red palace of the Dalai Lamas, with chapels, golden tombs and a thousand rooms climbing the hill.
items.expect: Tickets are timed and booked by your guide a day ahead; one hour is allowed inside; many stairs at high altitude.
items.tip: Walk the pilgrim circuit (kora) around the base at dawn, then see the palace from Chakpori hill at sunset.

items.name: Jokhang Temple
items.summary: The holiest temple in Tibet, home to the Jowo Shakyamuni statue, with pilgrims prostrating at its gates.
items.expect: Dim, crowded chapels lit by butter lamps; a rooftop with golden roofs and views of the Potala.
items.tip: Go in the morning when pilgrims fill the halls, and walk clockwise.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.

items.name: Barkhor Street
items.summary: The pilgrim circuit around the Jokhang, lined with stalls, teahouses and old Tibetan houses.
items.expect: A steady clockwise stream of pilgrims with prayer wheels and beads; security checkpoints at the entrances.
items.tip: Join the flow clockwise and stop at a rooftop café to watch.

items.name: Sera Monastery
items.summary: A great Gelug monastery where monks debate in a courtyard, clapping to make their points.
items.expect: The debates usually run in the afternoon on most weekdays.
items.tip: Ask your guide to time the visit for the debate, around 3 pm.

items.name: Ganden Monastery
items.summary: The mother monastery of the Gelug school, high on a ridge with a pilgrim path around it.
items.expect: About 1.5 hours by road; the kora takes an hour at 4,300 m.
items.tip: Save it for after you have adjusted to the altitude.

items.name: Yamdrok Lake
items.summary: A turquoise sacred lake below snow peaks, reached over the 4,900 m Kamba La pass.
items.expect: A full day trip, often on the way to Gyantse and Shigatse.
items.tip: Bring warm layers; it is windy at the pass.
